High throughput x‐ray astronomy Available

Many of the scientific objectives of x‐ray astronomy for the 1990’s and the twenty‐first century require high throughput. Three phases of high throughput telescopes are discussed: 1 m2, 10 m2, and 100 m2 effective areas. The era of the 1 m2 telescope will commence in the late 1990’s with the launches of XMM and LAMAR. A 10 m2 facility could be built with existing technology and launched as a free‐flyer on a rocket like the Soviet Energia. With its relevance to x‐ray astronomy’s scientific objectives the 10 m2 facility should be given high priority as the first major initiative of the twenty‐first century. A 100 m2 facility could occur in the middle of the twenty‐first century. Although it is rather speculative, an appropriate site for the 100 m2 telescope is a lunar base where x‐ray optics can be manufactured in situ.

Topics Telescopes, X-ray astronomy, X-ray optics, News and events
